files.notes.md:
Current implementation notes, synthetic project.
Each tenant has a monotonically increasing generation in Redis. Cache key=(tenant_id, item_id); cached object contains value and generation. Database is authoritative. TTL=60 seconds, unchanged. Reads compare the cached generation with the current tenant generation. Equal means return cached value; different or missing means fetch database.
Race: worker R reads database old value at generation 41. Worker W commits new DB value, then increments generation to 42. R attempts to cache old result after W. New code uses an atomic Redis script: write result only if current generation equals generation observed BEFORE fetching DB. Thus the stale R cache write is discarded. R still returns the database value it already fetched to its original caller. New code does not restart that original request. A later request sees generation mismatch/miss and fetches again.
DB commit and Redis increment are not one transaction. If increment fails, tenant cache reads are bypassed until the increment retry succeeds. This bypass is a tenant flag checked before cache lookup. Worker retries increment, not DB commit. Only this failure branch bypasses cache. This is deployed to staging, not production. Test: forced R/W interleaving passed 40/40. No production load measurement.
Implementation uses a Lua script; SET alone was used before. Cache hit metric is not a correctness proof. A generation is a tenant-wide change counter, not wall clock time. Generation increment invalidates all older entries for that tenant logically; it does not delete their keys.

files.notes.md:
Synthetic asynchronous export API. Current version.
POST /exports takes Idempotency-Key. Within one DB transaction, API inserts export job(state=queued) and outbox row. Only after commit returns 202 with job_id. 202 means durably accepted, not file ready. If DB transaction fails, neither row persists and API returns 503. Outbox dispatcher later publishes message to queue; publishing and marking row sent are not atomic. It can publish the same message again after a crash. Queue delivery is at least once. Worker claims queued job with conditional state update; only winner processes it. Result file stored before job changes to succeeded. GET /exports/{job_id} returns state and download URL only for succeeded. Failed includes error_code, no URL. Queued and running include no URL.
Key scope=(account_id, Idempotency-Key), retention24h measured from first accepted request, not refreshed by replay. Identical payload with same unexpired key returns same job_id and202, even if job already succeeded. Different payload with same unexpired key returns409. After24h a reused key can create new job. Another account may use same string independently. This does not promise exactly-once delivery. A failed job is not rerun by repeating POST with the same unexpired key and identical payload; the same job_id is returned. Client fetches GET for latest state.
An old design note proposed caching202 in gateway; that approach was not implemented. Polling interval/backoff is not specified. Current worker claim prevents simultaneous duplicate processing; crash recovery of an already-running worker is outside this note and must not be presented as solved.

files.notes.md:
Synthetic audit-log API, implemented v2.
Default order=(created_at DESC, id DESC), id breaks timestamp ties. First GET /logs creates snapshot of IDs matching filters and their order, retained15 minutes from creation. Response20 rows max + next_cursor. Cursor is opaque, signed token containing snapshot reference and position, not page number. Cursor request must reuse original filter values; changed filters with cursor gives400 FILTER_MISMATCH. To change filters start without cursor. Offset parameter not supported in v2.
New records after snapshot creation do not appear in that traversal; start a new first request to include them. ID set and order are frozen, field values are NOT frozen: for each response current row fields are read. A row deleted after snapshot is skipped; server scans further IDs until20 surviving rows or snapshot exhausted. Cursor advances past every scanned ID, including deleted ones. A page can have fewer than20 rows at exhaustion. No duplicates from equal timestamps within same traversal. This is not a historical archive. Permission is checked on every request, not frozen in snapshot; revoked access can cause403. Expired/unknown snapshot =>410 CURSOR_EXPIRED; client must discard cursor and start new traversal. Next_cursor=null means exhausted, not permission failure. Snapshot TTL is not extended by page requests.
Staging acceptance confirmed ties/deletes/filter mismatch/expiration; no offline export guarantee. Documentation draft used the phrase frozen data; it is misleading and must be reconciled with above implementation facts.

files.notes.md:
Synthetic migration from orders.total_text to orders.total_minor integer cents. USD only, no exchange conversion. PhaseA adds nullable total_minor; app v1 reads/writes total_text. PhaseB app v2 dual-writes both in SAME DB transaction, reads total_minor when non-null ELSE parses total_text; zero is valid and must not take fallback. Backfill processes IDs in ascending batches500; skips rows where total_minor already non-null; parsing invalid text records row in rejects, does not guess zero. B can coexist with v1 readers but all writers must be v2 BEFORE backfill starts, or old writers can update text without minor value. Current: schemaA and appv2 deployed; all writer instances confirmedv2; backfill paused after batch120. 60,000 rows scanned, 59,982 filled,18 rejects. Logs confirm rejects have invalid currency text. No data repairs yet. Remaining IDs exist after batch120; completion not established by60,000 count.
Resume command: python tools/backfill.py --after-batch 120 --batch-size 500 --resume
PhaseC switches app reads to total_minor only. Gate: all batches completed AND reject count zero AND parity comparison agrees for all rows. Current parity check has NOT run. Do not advance toC now. Repair rejected original values requires finance-owner confirmation, then rerun affected rows; supplied note gives no repair command. App rollback from B to v1 is possible while total_text is preserved and v2 dual writes continue until rollback completed. Do not drop total_text in B/C. PhaseD column removal only after separate approval; afterD, rollback to v1 needs restore/migration, not just binary rollback. No PhaseD date or approval exists.
User task is handoff only, not execute commands. Last CI72passes applies appv2, not backfill completion or parity.

files.notes.md:
Synthetic replay benchmark, not production rollout. Two versions same single8core machine; 10,000 HTTP requests EACH, serial runs; baseline first then cache version. Identical request sequence,90% reads/10% writes. Backend errors: baseline20/10000, cache10/10000; both HTTP5xx. Latency percentiles calculated ONLY successful requests: baseline9980, cache9990. Baseline p50=120ms,p95=600ms; cache p50=70ms,p95=650ms. Lowerp50 but higherp95. Do not call all requests faster. No repeated trials or confidence intervals. Load fixed100requests/sec; not throughput limit measured. No production data or multicore scaling benchmark.
Cache hits6300 among9000 reads=70%; not70%ofall10000requests. No cache lookups for writes. Database calls baseline9000, cache2700 for read path only. DB-call count is not total infrastructure cost. Redis cost and memory usage not measured. Cache TTL30s. Writes invalidate relevant cache entry after DB commit; invalidation failure count not captured. Dataset has no concurrent overwrite tests, so correctness of invalidation not established by low5xxrate. Improvement could depend on request order/warming; no randomized order. PM nextdecision is whether to run a production-like repeated benchmark, not approve rollout based on current evidence. Benchmark author proposed followup with concurrent writes and cost measurement; not yet performed. Do not invent expected savings or confidence.

files.notes.md:
Synthetic worker recovery policy, current approved procedure.
Begin by pausing intake: relayctl intake pause --queue image
Then inspect: relayctl status --queue image --json
Fields: pending_count integer or null; lease_renewal_ok boolean or null; dead_workers integer. pending_count null means telemetry unavailable, NOT0. lease_renewal_ok null means unknown, NOTfalse. Restart is allowed ONLY pending_count<=12 AND lease_renewal_ok=true AND dead_workers=0. If any required value unknown, keep intake paused, stop procedure, notify on-call lead. If known values fail any condition, keep intake paused, stop, notify on-call lead; no restart or automatic retry in this branch. Contact channel not specified.
Allowed restart command: relayctl workers restart --queue image --graceful
After restart inspect same status command. Recovery success ONLY pending_count=0 AND lease_renewal_ok=true AND dead_workers=0. Before restart <=12 threshold is NOT after-restart success threshold. If success, relayctl intake resume --queue image then record recovery complete. If not success or required values unknown, keep intake paused, stop and notify lead; do not repeat restart. A successful restart command exit is not recovery success. Resume before checking recovery is forbidden. If pause or status or restart command fails, stop and notify lead, do not assume the command took effect; no additional recovery command supplied.
The role reading this doc knows how to use shell and JSON, not relay internals. For numeric example boundary, pending12 qualifies before restart with other conditions; pending1 after restart is not success. This is one queue only. Do not claim all service recovery.
